boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten Fresno State places for studying, meeting, resetting between classes, viewing student art, and fitting movement into the day.

cards.title: Read the memorials, not just the map
cards.subtitle: A reflection space north of the Fresno State Library
cards.notes: Walk the garden slowly and read its memorials; the university identifies it as a setting for reflection, dialogue, and contemplation.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped campus gathering place centered on peace, activism, and considered conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: Fresno State says the Peace Garden is north of the Library and provides the campus community a serene place for reflection, contemplation, peaceful dialogue, and recognition of peace activists.
cards.access_notes: The official page describes campus-community use but does not publish opening hours; follow posted campus and event restrictions.

cards.title: Take the courtyard route through Conley
cards.subtitle: Murals, installations, trees, and student exhibitions
cards.notes: Cut through the courtyard when you want a visual reset, then check whether the Phebe Conley Art Gallery has a student exhibition installed.
cards.short_summary: A working arts building whose courtyard and gallery offer two different ways to pause between classes.
cards.evidence_claim: Fresno State Campus News documents murals and modern installations in the Conley Art Building, courtyard seating beneath trees, and rotating Art and Design student exhibitions in the Phebe Conley Art Gallery.
cards.source_title: 12 spaces on campus to find serenity
cards.access_notes: Building and gallery access may follow university schedules; verify current gallery access before planning an indoor visit.

cards.title: Move upstairs when you need a quieter pace
cards.subtitle: Third-floor reading space in the Fresno State Library
cards.notes: Bring reading or headphone work to the third floor; couches and tables make this useful when an event is not occupying the room.
cards.short_summary: A furnished library room suited to quiet reading and lower-intensity individual work.
cards.evidence_claim: Fresno State Campus News places the Table Mountain Rancheria Reading Room on the Library’s third floor and documents couches, tables, reading use, and availability when events are not occurring.
cards.source_title: 12 spaces on campus to find serenity
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to Fresno State Library hours and scheduled events; the source does not promise continuous room availability.

cards.title: Use the benches behind Alumni House
cards.subtitle: A demonstration garden designed with allergy concerns in mind
cards.notes: Find the garden behind Smittcamp Alumni House and use its benches for a short lunch or reset without claiming the planting is allergen-free for everyone.
cards.short_summary: A purpose-designed garden with seating and a location slightly removed from central pedestrian flow.
cards.evidence_claim: Fresno State Campus News identifies the Allergy-Free Demonstration Garden behind Smittcamp Alumni House, says it was designed to help people with hay fever and allergic asthma, and notes its benches.
cards.source_title: 12 spaces on campus to find serenity
cards.access_notes: The source does not provide hours or guarantee suitability for any individual allergy; observe signs and personal health needs.

cards.title: Look for the plant collection behind Science II
cards.subtitle: Teaching greenhouses with diverse tropical and ornamental plants
cards.notes: Approach from Science II and look for posted entry guidance before exploring; the documented collection includes orchids, ginger, coffee, and ferns.
cards.short_summary: A science-side destination where the university’s plant collection becomes visible outside a classroom.
cards.evidence_claim: Fresno State Campus News locates the greenhouses behind Science II and documents banana trees, begonias, orchids, coffee bushes, ginger, and ferns in the largest greenhouse.
cards.source_title: 12 spaces on campus to find serenity
cards.access_notes: The source describes the site but does not establish unrestricted interior access; obey posted greenhouse and laboratory controls.

cards.title: Claim a tier instead of another indoor chair
cards.subtitle: Outdoor tiered seating at the Resnick Student Union
cards.notes: Use the tiered plaza for a between-class pause or informal meetup, leaving event routes and any reserved sections clear.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor extension of the student union built around stepped seating, grass, and evening lighting.
cards.evidence_claim: Fresno State Campus News identifies the Leon S. Peters Event Plaza at the Resnick Student Union as an outdoor tiered seating area with cement seating, grass, and embedded lights.
cards.source_title: 12 spaces on campus to find serenity
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access can be affected by university events or reservations; follow barriers, signs, and campus access rules.

cards.title: Take the dry-river-bed route
cards.subtitle: A designed walkway in front of the Resnick Student Union
cards.notes: Use the pathway for a deliberate lap between tasks, noticing the dry-river-bed design rather than treating it only as a shortcut.
cards.short_summary: A short designed walking route that turns circulation space into a momentary mental reset.
cards.evidence_claim: Fresno State Campus News places Reflection Pathway south of the fountain and in front of the Resnick Student Union, describing its dry-river-bed design and intended use as a peaceful walkway.
cards.source_title: 12 spaces on campus to find serenity
cards.access_notes: The official feature does not list hours; use the outdoor path only when surrounding campus grounds are open and unobstructed.

cards.title: Find the brick booths north of the USU
cards.subtitle: Outdoor seating between the student union and McLane Hall
cards.notes: Bring lunch or a short reading assignment to the brick seating booths, and keep shared tables available for other campus users.
cards.short_summary: A cluster of outdoor seats that supports lunch, reading, and small conversations near busy academic buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: Fresno State Campus News locates the University Student Union Courtyard Plaza north of the USU and beside McLane Hall, documenting numerous outdoor seats and brick seating booths.
cards.source_title: 12 spaces on campus to find serenity
cards.access_notes: The outdoor plaza may be affected by events or campus closures; no dedicated hours are stated on the supporting page.

cards.entity_name: Lynda and Stewart Resnick Student Union
cards.title: Match the floor to the task
cards.subtitle: Indoor seating, outdoor seating, meeting rooms, and the Den
cards.notes: Choose among first-, second-, or limited third-floor seating; reserve a meeting room or the Den’s Peace Room when your task needs one.
cards.short_summary: A multi-level student hub where solo work, club meetings, meals, and quiet reflection have separate options.
cards.evidence_claim: The current Student Unions page documents indoor and outdoor seating at the Resnick Student Union, reservable club meeting rooms, and a reservable Peace Room in the Den for study, prayer, or meditation.
cards.access_notes: Meeting rooms and the Peace Room require reservations; use other areas during posted Resnick Student Union operating hours.

cards.title: Put movement between two study blocks
cards.subtitle: Campus recreation facility at 5010 N. Woodrow Avenue
cards.notes: Check eligibility and facility schedules before arriving, then use the center to separate long academic work periods with purposeful movement.
cards.short_summary: A student-focused recreation facility that supports fitness, wellness, employment, and leadership experience.
cards.evidence_claim: Fresno State identifies the Student Recreation Center as a university-community facility providing recreational and fitness opportunities and student development and leadership opportunities.
cards.access_notes: Access is eligibility-controlled; consult current membership rules and facility schedules before visiting. The page lists 5010 N. Woodrow Ave.
